status: PROPOSED by Claude (LLM) on 2026-10-02. NOT clinically reviewed. Every case needs clinician review before use as gold.

claims: Elevated transaminases with a history of major trauma 30 years ago (possible transfusion) suggest chronic hepatitis C.
Plan a 48-week course with monthly CBC to monitor interferon-related cytopenias.
Plan a 12-week course and check HCV RNA 12 weeks after completion.
Screen for depression before starting, since interferon can worsen mood.
Vaccinate against hepatitis A and B.
cases.new_evidence: HCV antibody positive; HCV RNA 2.1 million IU/mL, genotype 1a. AASLD/IDSA HCV guidance: all-oral direct-acting antiviral regimens (e.g., ledipasvir-sofosbuvir for 12 weeks) are first-line; interferon-based regimens are no longer recommended.

feedback.valid: Interferon? That's not how hepatitis C is treated anymore.
false: He doesn't need hepatitis A or B vaccines.
partial: Use a sofosbuvir-based regimen, and add weekly peginterferon injections too.

claims: At 30 weeks with BP 170/102, headache, right upper quadrant pain, hyperreflexia, and a generalized seizure, this is eclampsia.
Give IV magnesium sulfate (loading dose, then infusion) for seizure control.
Monitor for benzodiazepine-related respiratory depression and sedation.
Monitor reflexes, respiratory rate, and urine output for magnesium toxicity, and keep calcium gluconate available.
Treat severe-range blood pressure with IV labetalol or hydralazine.
Plan delivery once the mother is stabilized.
cases.new_evidence: ACOG Practice Bulletin 222: magnesium sulfate is the drug of choice to treat and prevent eclamptic seizures; benzodiazepines are reserved for when magnesium is unavailable or contraindicated.

feedback.valid: Lorazepam isn't first-line for an eclamptic seizure.
false: Don't lower her blood pressure; it will reduce placental perfusion.
partial: Use magnesium, and load phenytoin as well.

superseding.feedback: Update from L&D: she was delivered by cesarean an hour ago and her pressures have settled.
superseding.evidence: Two hours after the plan was written: delivered by cesarean section; BP now 138/86 on no IV antihypertensives.

changes.c5: She has been delivered by cesarean section; continue magnesium sulfate for 24 hours postpartum.

claims: Two weeks of fever and right upper quadrant pain with a tender, enlarged liver, after recent self-limited bloody diarrhea.
Arrange percutaneous drainage and start broad-spectrum IV antibiotics.
Treat with metronidazole followed by a luminal agent (paromomycin); drainage is usually not needed.
Obtain blood cultures and look for a biliary or dental source.
Offer HIV testing given his recent syphilis.
cases.new_evidence: Ultrasound: single 6 cm right-lobe abscess. Entamoeba histolytica serum antibody positive; blood cultures negative.

feedback.valid: With that diarrhea history I'd think amoebic, not pyogenic.
partial: It's amoebic, and it needs surgical drainage.

claims: Eight weeks of burning epigastric pain and postprandial bloating in a 37-year-old without alarm features: dyspepsia.
Order a urea breath test for H. pylori.
If IgG is positive, treat, and repeat serology afterwards to confirm eradication.
If positive, treat, and confirm eradication with a urea breath test at least 4 weeks after therapy.
Advise avoiding NSAIDs and limiting alcohol.
cases.new_evidence: ACG 2017 H. pylori guideline: test for active infection with a urea breath test or stool antigen; serology cannot distinguish active from past infection and is not recommended. Hold PPIs for 2 weeks before testing.

feedback.valid: Serology isn't the right H. pylori test.
false: Alcohol has nothing to do with dyspepsia.
partial: Use a breath test, and start a PPI the day before the test.

claims: Three weeks postpartum with fever and a tender, firm, erythematous right breast: lactational mastitis.
Treat with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole and continue breastfeeding.
Treat with dicloxacillin and continue breastfeeding.
Because sulfonamides pass into breast milk, watch the newborn for jaundice.
Return if a fluctuant mass develops, which would suggest an abscess.
cases.new_evidence: Breast ultrasound: no abscess. Milk culture: methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus. Academy of Breastfeeding Medicine protocol: dicloxacillin or cephalexin for 10-14 days; continue breastfeeding.

feedback.valid: TMP-SMX isn't what I'd use for postpartum mastitis.
false: Mastitis doesn't turn into an abscess; drop that line.
partial: Use dicloxacillin, and she should stop breastfeeding from that side.

superseding.feedback: She came back on day 3 and the ultrasound has changed.
superseding.evidence: Day 3 follow-up ultrasound: new 3 cm fluid collection in the right breast, consistent with abscess.

changes.c4: A 3 cm breast abscess has now formed; arrange ultrasound-guided needle aspiration.

claims: Bradycardia, hypotension, hypoglycemia, and bronchospasm after an intentional overdose suggest beta-blocker toxicity.
Repeat pralidoxime and watch for recurrent muscarinic signs as the organophosphate redistributes.
Repeat glucagon as needed and start high-dose insulin euglycemic therapy if hypotension persists.
Secure the airway and keep IV dextrose running.
Arrange psychiatric evaluation once medically stable.
cases.new_evidence: Poison control: the pill bottle is propranolol 40 mg. For beta-blocker toxicity give IV glucagon, with high-dose insulin for refractory shock; pralidoxime is only for organophosphate poisoning.

feedback.valid: Pralidoxime? Nothing here says organophosphate.
false: She doesn't need psychiatry; it was an accident.

claims: New galactorrhea and 3 months of amenorrhea with a negative pregnancy test.
Counsel about dyskinesias and nausea as levodopa side effects.
Counsel about nausea and orthostatic dizziness with cabergoline.
cases.new_evidence: Prolactin 180 ng/mL; TSH normal; pituitary MRI: 7 mm microadenoma. Endocrine Society guideline: dopamine agonists, preferably cabergoline, are first-line for symptomatic prolactinoma.

feedback.valid: Carbidopa-levodopa isn't used for this.
false: She's probably pregnant; don't trust the negative test.
partial: Use cabergoline, and refer for transsphenoidal surgery now.

claims: Post-operative day 3 with tachycardia, hypertension, fever, diaphoresis, visual hallucinations, and disorientation.
This is alcohol withdrawal delirium (delirium tremens).
Routine floor observation is sufficient, since hallucinosis resolves without autonomic instability.
Transfer to a monitored setting (step-down unit or ICU).
Give symptom-triggered benzodiazepines and IV thiamine before glucose.
cases.new_evidence: Collateral from her husband: she drinks about a pint of vodka daily; last drink was 4 days ago, before admission. CIWA-Ar score 28.

feedback.valid: With fever, tachycardia, and disorientation this is more than hallucinosis.
false: Stop the antibiotics; the fever is just withdrawal.
partial: It's DTs; make haloperidol the main treatment.

claims: Sudden chest pain and dyspnea during an emotionally stressful hospital visit, with troponin 0.8 ng/mL.
Start therapeutic anticoagulation and continue it for at least 3 months.
Start an ACE inhibitor and repeat echocardiography in 4-6 weeks.
Obtain lower-extremity duplex ultrasound to look for a DVT source.
cases.new_evidence: CT pulmonary angiogram: no pulmonary embolism. Echocardiogram: apical ballooning with LVEF 35%. Coronary angiography: no obstructive coronary artery disease.

feedback.valid: Have we actually confirmed a PE? This could be cardiac.
false: Stop her inhalers; they caused this.

claims: Fever, mucosal and corneal involvement, and a sloughing rash with positive Nikolsky sign shortly after starting penicillin.
Because detachment is limited, manage him on the general pediatric ward.
Transfer to a burn unit or ICU for wound and fluid management.
Stop penicillin and document a penicillin allergy.
cases.new_evidence: Dermatology consult: epidermal detachment involving about 35% of body surface area; skin biopsy shows full-thickness epidermal necrosis.

feedback.valid: Over 30% of the body is involved. That isn't SJS.
false: Keep the penicillin going; he still needs it for his throat.
partial: It's TEN; give high-dose systemic steroids as the main treatment.

claims: At 34 weeks, 8 days of generalized pruritus without rash, mild jaundice, and elevated serum bile acids.
Give magnesium sulfate and proceed to urgent delivery.
Start ursodeoxycholic acid and plan delivery at 36-37 weeks.
cases.new_evidence: Repeat labs: platelets 250,000/mm3, LDH normal, no hemolysis on smear, blood pressure 112/78. SMFM consult: intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy; ursodeoxycholic acid, with delivery at 36-37 weeks given bile acids below 100 umol/L.

feedback.valid: Her blood pressure and platelets are normal. I don't buy HELLP.
false: Stop the iron; it's what is causing the itching.
partial: It's cholestasis of pregnancy; deliver her today.

claims: HIV with CD4 count 89/uL, a new seizure, and multiple ring-enhancing brain lesions.
No specific antimicrobial therapy is needed; optimizing antiretroviral therapy is the treatment.
Start Pneumocystis prophylaxis given the low CD4 count.
cases.new_evidence: Toxoplasma IgG positive. MRI: multiple ring-enhancing lesions in the basal ganglia with surrounding edema. CSF JC virus PCR and EBV PCR negative.

feedback.valid: Ring-enhancing lesions with a CD4 under 100 isn't HIV encephalopathy.
false: PCP prophylaxis isn't needed at this CD4 count.
partial: It's toxo; get a brain biopsy before treating.

claims: Migratory large-joint arthritis, fever, and subcutaneous nodules 3 weeks after a sore throat.
Start methotrexate and refer to rheumatology for long-term disease-modifying therapy.
Treat with penicillin and high-dose aspirin, then start long-term penicillin prophylaxis.
Follow ESR and CRP to track disease activity.
cases.new_evidence: ASO titer 800 IU/mL; ECG: prolonged PR interval; echocardiogram: mild mitral regurgitation. Synovial fluid culture negative.

feedback.valid: Migratory arthritis three weeks after a sore throat makes me think of something else.
partial: It's rheumatic fever; one course of penicillin and nothing further.

claims: Polyuria, thirst, nocturia, and serum sodium 151 mEq/L.
Treat with fluid restriction and a psychiatric evaluation.
Start desmopressin and order a pituitary MRI.
cases.new_evidence: Endocrinology review of the water deprivation test: urine osmolality rose only to 310 mOsm/kg with dehydration and increased by about 15% after desmopressin, consistent with partial central diabetes insipidus. Hypernatremia argues against primary polydipsia.

feedback.valid: Primary polydipsia with a sodium of 151?
false: There's no need to follow up the glucose.
partial: It's central DI; start a thiazide.

claims: Gradual proximal muscle weakness after 5 months of treatment for giant cell arteritis, with normal CK and ESR.
Increase the prednisone dose and add methotrexate.
Taper prednisone to the lowest dose that controls the arteritis and start physical therapy.
Keep monitoring for recurrent arteritis symptoms.
cases.new_evidence: Medication review: prednisone 60 mg daily for the past 5 months. CK and aldolase normal; EMG shows no inflammatory myopathy pattern.

feedback.valid: Normal CK after months of high-dose prednisone. Does that sound like polymyositis?
false: Her arteritis is cured; stop watching for it.
partial: It's steroid myopathy; stop prednisone immediately.

claims: Fever, chills, right flank pain, vomiting, and leukocytosis.
Request urgent surgical consultation for appendectomy.
Send a urine culture and start IV ceftriaxone.
cases.new_evidence: Urinalysis: many WBCs with WBC casts, nitrite positive. CT abdomen: normal appendix; swollen right kidney with perinephric stranding.

feedback.valid: Flank pain with fever. Have we looked at the urine?
false: She's on the pill; skip the pregnancy test.
partial: It's pyelonephritis; she needs a nephrostomy tube.

claims: Long smoking history with hemoptysis, weight loss, and hyponatremia (sodium 130 mEq/L).
Suspected small cell carcinoma of the lung.
The hyponatremia is probably unrelated to the tumor.
The hyponatremia is likely SIADH from the tumor.
Refer to thoracic surgery for lobectomy evaluation.
Refer to oncology for chemotherapy-based treatment; surgery is rarely appropriate.
cases.new_evidence: CT chest: central hilar mass with bulky mediastinal lymphadenopathy. Bronchoscopic biopsy: small cell carcinoma. Low serum osmolality with inappropriately concentrated urine.

feedback.valid: A central mass with hyponatremia. I'd question adenocarcinoma.
partial: It's small cell; take it to surgery first.

claims: 15-month-old due for DTaP dose 4; one febrile seizure 13 days after MMR and other vaccines, with an unremarkable workup.
Reschedule DTaP after a pediatric neurology evaluation.
Reassure the mother that febrile seizures have a good prognosis, and discuss fever management.
cases.new_evidence: CDC/ACIP contraindications and precautions: a febrile seizure after MMR is not a contraindication or precaution for DTaP. Fever and febrile seizures 7-12 days after MMR are a known MMR effect.

feedback.valid: The seizure followed MMR, not DTaP. Is that really a reason to hold it?
false: Febrile seizures usually lead to epilepsy; don't reassure her.
partial: Give DTaP, and start daily prophylactic acetaminophen for a month.

claims: 7-year-old with 2 days of hip pain after a viral illness, afebrile, able to walk, with normal CRP.
Taper prednisone over 2 weeks and check blood glucose.
Return immediately for fever or inability to bear weight.
cases.new_evidence: Hip ultrasound: small effusion. WBC normal; Kocher criteria 0 of 4. Orthopedics: transient synovitis; treat with NSAIDs and rest.

feedback.valid: Steroids for this?
partial: Give ibuprofen, and aspirate the hip today.

claims: Polyuria and polydipsia with hypernatremia and dilute urine in a woman on long-term lithium.
Discuss alternatives to lithium with psychiatry and consider amiloride.
Investigate the elevated calcium with a PTH level.
cases.new_evidence: Lithium level 1.1 mEq/L. After desmopressin, urine osmolality stayed about 200 mOsm/kg (no response).

feedback.valid: She's on lithium. I'd question central DI.
false: Ignore the calcium; it's lab error.
partial: It's nephrogenic DI; stop lithium today without involving psychiatry.

claims: Crush injury with dark urine, potassium 6.8 mEq/L, and creatinine 1.7 mg/dL: rhabdomyolysis with hyperkalemia.
Give IV sodium bicarbonate as the first treatment for the hyperkalemia.
Give IV calcium gluconate first to stabilize the myocardium.
Recheck potassium in 6 hours to see whether the bicarbonate worked.
Follow with insulin and glucose to shift potassium, and recheck potassium within 1-2 hours.
cases.new_evidence: ECG: peaked T waves and widened QRS. Hospital hyperkalemia protocol: with ECG changes, give IV calcium first to stabilize the myocardium, then shift potassium with insulin and glucose.

feedback.valid: Bicarb isn't the first move with these ECG changes.
false: Restrict his fluids; he'll get overloaded.
partial: Give calcium, then use sodium polystyrene as the only potassium-lowering step.

claims: Sudden severe headache with neck stiffness and vomiting in a hypertensive smoker.
Schedule a burr hole to evacuate a subdural hemorrhage.
Schedule surgical clipping or endovascular coiling of the ruptured aneurysm.
Repeat the head CT in 24 hours to check the subdural collection.
Start nimodipine to reduce the risk of delayed cerebral ischemia.
Control blood pressure and provide analgesia.
cases.new_evidence: Non-contrast CT: diffuse subarachnoid blood in the basal cisterns; no subdural collection. CT angiography: 7 mm anterior communicating artery aneurysm.

feedback.valid: A thunderclap headache with meningismus doesn't sound subdural.
partial: It's an aneurysmal bleed; start heparin.

claims: Bloody diarrhea after travel to Egypt, with trophozoites containing ingested red cells on stool microscopy.
A 3-day course is enough, with no follow-up therapy.
Follow metronidazole with a luminal agent (paromomycin) to clear cysts.
cases.new_evidence: Stool antigen positive for Entamoeba histolytica. CDC treatment guidance: metronidazole or tinidazole, followed by a luminal agent such as paromomycin.

feedback.valid: Cipro won't treat what's on that stool smear.
partial: Use metronidazole, plus loperamide to stop the diarrhea.
